column6: The proof now exists and is truthful: a run is decided only after its send outcome is known, its step log names the send step and the recipient, exactly one email is delivered per run, and a failed send reads FAILED with the reason. One blocker remains and it is not in this lane. Saving a workflow through the builder rewrites the automation's trigger from the dotted form the runtime matcher uses to an underscored form, so the automation silently stops firing altogether and produces no run at all. An admin who builds and publishes on the canvas therefore still gets nothing, even though everything downstream of the trigger is now correct.

The mail catcher received exactly 1 message with the matching subject. Its outbox row read status=dispatched, attempts=1. column9: MEASURED LIVE before the fix. The step log column was empty for every run, so a run showed that something happened but never what. The run verdict was written before and independently of the action outcome, so a run whose send failed still read completed. An unrecognised step type returned a 'message' key rather than an 'error' key, and since the executor only fails a step on 'error', five action types the API happily accepts - send_sms, api_request, classify_record, enrich_record and generate_summary - all recorded a success having done nothing. On the durable path the close-out wrote its reason to run.error, which is not a column on that model, so the assignment silently created a throwaway Python attribute and every durable failure was stored with no reason at all.

column4: I want missing inputs, generation failures, and timeouts handled gracefully and shown, so that a failed AI step doesn't silently break my automation.
column6: Scoped to the stuck-pending half of this story only, which is the part this lane owns. Runs no longer hang: every run now reaches a decided outcome, whether it succeeded, failed, or was abandoned mid-flight. The AI-specific half is untouched here and remains unproven - agent steps are still rejected by the authoring validator so they cannot be published at all, and nothing in this work addresses how a generation failure or model timeout is worded or surfaced to the user.
column7: RAN LIVE. (1) NOTHING HANGS ANY MORE: across the whole session every automation run created in the preceding hour ended in a terminal state - a status count over that window returned only completed and failed, with zero rows in pending, running or queued. (2) CRASHED RUNS GET AN OUTCOME: with the mail catcher stopped mid-run, run 94f5b1c2 moved queued -> failed within about ten seconds carrying the real transport error, rather than sitting queued. (3) THE BUILDER PATH NO LONGER HANGS: run 9fd422ea went running -> completed in 5356 ms, where the identical automation previously stayed on running indefinitely because every action step died on a missing module. (4) BACKSTOP: a new reaper writes a failure onto any run abandoned without an outcome. It is deliberately conservative - it leaves recent runs alone, leaves runs whose email is still in flight alone, and for a durable run it asks Temporal whether the workflow is still going, only deciding runs whose workflow is definitively gone; if Temporal cannot be reached it leaves the run alone so an outage never reports a failure for work still happening. AUTOMATICALLY TESTED: 6 tests covering exactly those branches pass against a real Postgres database.

column9: MEASURED LIVE before the fix. Every run on the builder path stayed on 'running' forever because each action step raised ModuleNotFoundError for a handler module that has never existed, so the workflow never reached the step that closes the run - observed live as a run still on running 150 s after a 5-second wait. On top of that, the durable close-out wrote its failure reason to a non-existent attribute, so even when a run was closed the reason was discarded. And nothing existed to decide a run whose process died between creation and completion, so such a run stayed un-decided permanently.

column11: Expected: an AI step that lacks an input, fails to generate, or times out is handled and shown, and never leaves the automation in limbo. Actual: the limbo half is fixed and proven - runs always reach an outcome and a failure always carries its reason. The AI half is genuinely not addressed: agent steps cannot currently be published because the authoring validator rejects that node type, so there is no live path on which to observe a generation failure or timeout at all.
column12: 1) Owned by the step-execution lane: give the agent step real handling for a missing input, a generation failure and a timeout, each with a message that names what was missing rather than a raw exception. 2) Owned by the authoring lane: allow the agent node to be published once it can actually execute, since today it is rejected at save time. 3) Re-run this story end to end once an agent step can be published, and confirm each of the three failure shapes lands in the run's step log with a readable reason.
